abdominal-etching-high-definition-lipo.text: Users who are lean but lack visible abs choose it to sculpt the lines of the abdominal muscles, so a six-pack shows without further fat loss. The visible change is the result itself; evidence comes from surgeon case series and one systematic review rather than randomized trials.

lymph-sparing-liposuction.text: It is a liposuction method developed for lipedema, where excess leg fat is removed while protecting lymphatics, so the main use is medical rather than cosmetic. Appearance-minded readers see it as a way to slim the legs; reported outcomes are positive but from limited studies.

chain: Fat cells die off over weeks
coolsculpting-elite.text: People use fat freezing to shrink stubborn pockets such as the belly or flanks and sharpen body contour without surgery. Studies document modest local fat reduction over a few weeks; a rare paradoxical fat-growth complication is also documented.

cooltone.text: It is discussed as an add-on to fat freezing, with the idea that magnetic contractions tone the area so the result looks firmer and more defined. The tone claim rests on manufacturer marketing; almost no published evidence exists for the device itself.

chain: Forced muscle contractions plus RF heat
emsculpt-neo.text: Users take it to firm and slim areas like the abs, glutes, thighs and arms by combining muscle contractions with fat heating. Reviews report fat reduction and muscle gains, though many studies use the same device and often come from the maker's circle.

chain: RF heats skin, stimulates facial muscles
emface.text: It is promoted as a needle-free way to smooth wrinkles and lift the face over a short course of sessions. The headline improvement figures come mainly from manufacturer-supported studies.

trusculpt-id.text: Users consider it for non-invasive slimming of localized fat on areas such as the abdomen. Many small trials are registered, but few published results are available for this specific device.

cavitation-ultrasonic-fat.text: Forum users, especially for DIY face slimming, use cavitation devices hoping to spot-reduce fat in the cheeks and jaw area. Only small registered trials exist and no cosmetic results were located for the home-use claim.

endermologie-lpg.text: It is used to soften the look of cellulite and improve body contour through machine massage. Small studies report contour and texture changes; large controlled evidence is limited.

qwo-collagenase.text: It is an injectable approved for cellulite dimples on women's buttocks, aimed at a smoother look of the area. Clinical trials studied dimple improvement, with bruising the main studied concern.

ultrasound-skin-tightening.text: People use microfocused ultrasound such as Ulthera to lift sagging skin on the jawline, neck and brows without surgery. Published cohort studies exist for face and neck; detailed effect sizes were not verified here.

microneedling-skinpen.text: It is used for acne scars, wrinkles and overall texture, sometimes combined with platelet-rich plasma. Several small trials on scars, wrinkles and acne are registered for SkinPen; published results were not located here.

dermastamp.text: Looksmax forum users stamp skin, under-eye lines and brows, sometimes alongside minoxidil, hoping for smoother skin and fuller brows. Microneedling generally has studies, but no cosmetic trials of the stamp itself were found.

jet-peel-needle-free.text: Clinics offer it as a needle-free facial for hydration and a smoother look. Little has been published on it.

hydrafacial-keravive.text: It is pitched as a salon scalp facial for scalp health and hair quality. The hair appearance claim is based on marketing; only registered studies exist, with no published results.

oxygen-facial.text: People get it before events for immediate hydration and a glow with no downtime. Serum ingredients like hyaluronic acid are studied on their own; no trials of the oxygen treatment itself exist.

led-light-facial.text: It is used in clinics and at home for acne and skin ageing, with blue light aimed at acne and red/near-infrared at texture. Small trials show preliminary results.

dermalinfusion.text: It is used to exfoliate and infuse serums, notably for dark marks in skin of color. The evidence found is a single small 2014 study on post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation.

chain: Acid mix sheds top skin layer
jessner-peel.text: It is a superficial peel used for fine lines, acne marks and uneven pigment, and to prime skin before deeper TCA or retinoic peels. Evidence specific to Jessner's solution is limited.

chain: Fewer scars, even tone, fewer lines
tca-peel.text: It is a medium-depth clinic peel used for scars, pigment and sun damage. Decades of small clinical studies cover these uses.

vi-peel.text: It is a branded medium peel marketed for acne, pigment, sun damage and fine lines across skin tones. Published data are a few small studies.

obagi-blue-peel.text: It is a branded TCA peel designed to be deeper than superficial peels while keeping depth predictable. Its published record is thin, including a 1999 paper describing the standardized method.

pca-peel.text: It is a line of professional chemical peels sold by PCA Skin for general skin renewal and pigment concerns. The claims come from the manufacturer and independent published trials were not found.

cosmelan-peel.text: It is used for melasma, dark marks and sun spots in a clinic mask phase followed by months of home care. Claims come from the manufacturer; no published trials were found.

dermamelan.text: Appearance communities discuss it as a way to even out skin tone and fade melasma. Support is limited to one small pilot study.

retinol-peel-retinoic-acid-peel.text: It is used for photoaging, scars, wrinkles and pigment. A few small trials exist for photoaging and acanthosis nigricans, with no consensus protocol.

salicylic-acid-peel.text: It is the superficial peel most often used for acne and pigmentation. Small comparative studies support its acne use.

glycolic-acid-peel.text: It is the most widely studied AHA peel, used for melasma, dark under-eyes, acne scars and fine lines. Studies are mostly small.

lactic-acid-peel.text: It is used as a gentle peel for dark under-eye circles and melasma. A few small comparisons exist.

mandelic-acid-peel.text: It is promoted as a gentle peel for people across age groups and skin tones. Only two small studies stand behind it.
